## 共同的问题

| 编号 | 问题 | 证据 | 影响 | 处理 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | 判官看不到被测系统拿到的材料，也看不到系统自己的代码和产出 | PaperWritingBench 的 SxS 只读两篇论文（官方 `sxs_paper_quality.py`、`sxs_lit_review_quality.py`）；PaperWrite-Bench 的幻觉检查只拿原论文 LaTeX 对照（`evaluate_per_section.py` 的 pass 1）；ResearchClawBench 的判官只读报告、checklist 和图（`evaluation/score.py`） | 系统自己补出的方法细节、记错方法的数字、没有代码算过的数字都发现不了，有时还被当作优点加分（P1） | 新增 `faithfulness-judge`：逐条核对文档对自身工作的陈述与材料（和评测侧的参照）是否一致。验证见 P1、W3、R1 |
| C2 | 判官模型被替换，且去掉了采样参数 | Gemini `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` 由 Antigravity 以 `gemini-4-argon-high` 服务；GPT 判官（`gpt-4o`、`gpt-5`、`gpt-5.1`、`gpt-5.4`）由 codex-api 以 `gpt-5.6-sol`、effort medium 服务；`temperature`、`top_p` 被去掉（`codex_api.toml`） | 判官的宽严和波动可能与官方不同 | 每条分数记录实际服务的模型。替代判官有锚点：PaperWritingBench 原论文对其逐字节副本的 SxS 8 次全平（#42 调查）；ScienceAgentBench 图像判官对全部图像题做了 gold、他题 gold、空白三种锚点（S5）；ResearchClawBench 同一报告重复打分（R5） |
| C3 | 一次打分会波动 | ResearchClawBench 同一份报告五次打分在 23.7 和 29.3 之间（R5）；PaperWrite-Bench 同一份论文（运行 R2）重新打分，rubric 3.56 变 3.61、重大幻觉 1 条变 4 条、claim 241 条变 227 条（本 Issue）；PaperWritingBench 同一篇论文（运行 `…-20261028T002600Z`）的文献综述 #42 打 58 / 57（Gemini / GPT），本 Issue 重新打分 51 / 52；SxS 的胜负两次相同 | 单题、单次的差几分不说明问题 | ResearchClawBench 每次打分另打 2 次，报告均值、标准差和极差（`project_checks.repeats`）；其余两项单次打分要 20 次以上调用，只在汇总上比较 |
| C4 | 离线题不是完全断网：屏蔽放行 Python 包索引 | PaperWrite-Bench 的官方写作 agent 没有网络工具，ASI-Bench 榜单页写“没有外部工具访问”，PhysClosureBench 的 `network_access` 是 `disabled`；本项目这三个 benchmark 的题目以 `offline` 屏蔽运行，另放行 `pypi.org/simple/` 和 `files.pythonhosted.org/packages/` 的 `GET`/`HEAD`（设置 `shield.package_index`，每次运行的 `setup.network` 写 `package_index: allowed`，#105） | 被测系统能 pip 装包，官方 agent 不能；包索引不含题目答案，也不含论文内容，其他站点（文献、论文、代码托管、搜索）照旧 403，屏蔽表（原论文、仓库）先于放行生效 | 记入每次运行的记录和看板；不改官方评分；读离线题的结果时按此条理解联网条件 |

## PaperWrite-Bench（`paperwritebench-judge`）

| 编号 | 问题 | 证据 | 影响 | 处理 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | Citation F1 大部分来自给系统的 `references.bib` | 把给的 bib 里每个键都引用一遍、一个字不写，F1 在全部 51 篇上均值 0.756、中位数 0.838（子集 25 篇均值 0.760、中位数 0.869）；`paper_13` 的这个基线 0.613，两次运行 0.673、0.646 | F1 主要衡量“少引了 bib 里的哪些”，不衡量写作 | `project_checks.citation`：全引基线、高出基线的部分、去掉注释里的 `\cite` 后重算（官方正则也算注释里的键） |
| W2 | 幻觉的主指标是原始计数，原论文没写的内容记为 neutral、不核对 | 官方 `total_contradictory_major` 是计数（`evaluate_per_section.py`），没有归一化；运行 R2（`coding-agent-paperwritebench--paper_13-20261028T002540Z`）241 条 claim、31 条 neutral；同一份论文重新打分是 227 条、37 条 neutral，major 从 1 条变 4 条 | 论文越短、claim 越少越占便宜；编造原论文没提的内容不扣分 | `project_checks.hallucination`：每百条 claim 的 major、minor、neutral；材料依据见 W3 |
| W3 | 幻觉检查看不到材料，正确的内容被判为重大幻觉 | 运行 R1（`…-20261027T230211Z`）唯一的 major 是“生成的描述明确说出了 gyoza”，而给系统的图 `figures/description_eg.jpg` 上就印着 “there is a large plate featuring gyoza”；复核 agent 只读了原论文 LaTeX，没有改判。运行 R2 的 major 是“Task 3 的模型身份无法确定”：给系统的 `table_vs.tex` 的基线行与 `table_kf.tex` 的 Qwen2-VL-7B 行完全相同、却标作 Qwen2.5-VL-7B，系统照实写出了这处不一致。R2 重新打分得到的 4 条 major 里仍有这两条（gyoza 和模型身份），另两条是“距类中心 1.5 个标准差”对“高于类均值 1.5 个标准差”和从图上读出的曲线数值 | 每篇 0–1 个 major 基本是噪声，诚实报告材料里的不一致反而被扣分 | `faithfulness-judge`（材料含图和表，参照是原论文 LaTeX）：R2 的这两条 GPT 和 Gemini 都判为有材料依据；GPT 121 条实证陈述里 9 条无依据或矛盾、0 条重大（“只跑了一次”“没有测一致性”等措辞），Gemini 44 条全部有依据 |
| W4 | rubric 和幻觉检查的范围由章节标题决定 | 官方按关键词把章节分类（`evaluate_per_section.py`）；`paper_13` 的原论文没有 Experiment 类，R2 写在 “Results and Analysis” 下的结果不进 rubric，要素 “Main classification benchmark finding” 得 1 分（“No classification results are reported”）；Conclusion/Discussion 类和不足 50 词的章节不做幻觉检查 | 照抄原论文的章节结构能多得分，放进 Discussion 的内容不受检查 | 标注（改分类就改了官方评分） |
| W5 | rubric 按原论文的要素给分，不核对是否正确，没有长度约束 | 要素来自原论文（`eval_points`）；官方评分不检查页数 | 写得多、贴近原论文结构的论文占便宜 | 标注 |
| W6 | 复核 agent 只能把 contradictory 改小，且和被测系统同一家族 | 复核只看 contradictory 的 claim；Claude Code `claude-sonnet-4-6` 复核，被测的 coding agent 是 `claude-sonnet-5-5`；复核时工作目录里同时有预测稿和 `gt_main.tex` | 自偏好未测量 | 标注；判官和复核模型写在分数里 |
| W7 | `--eval-mode all` 下复核抛错会让整次评测没有结果文件 | 官方 `all` 模式的 pass 2 没有 try/except，`hallucination` 模式有 | 打分失败而不是部分结果 | 我们的评测系统在没有结果文件时报 `ScoreUnavailable`，不写分数；重新打分即可 |
| W8 | 题目要求的会议样式文件，官方仓库和数据集都没有发布 | 51 篇的模板用 `neurips_2025`、`cvpr`、`iclr2025_conference` 等 14 个样式文件，数据集、PaperRecon 仓库和标准 TeX Live 都没有；干净 TeX Live 里 46 篇编译不过；官方 `generated_papers/` 的 PDF 却是会议排版，官方环境从哪取得样式查不到（#113）；已有的 `paper_1` 运行里，各系统拿到的目录没有样式文件，有的用自己写的占位样式、有的换了模板（见 benchmark README） | 官方评分只读 `template.tex` 的文本，所以不改分数的算法；影响的是系统能否按模板编译，以及没有样式时排版和页数不是官方版式 | 新增候选输入：按模板用到的名字，把各会议官方公开的样式包文件（资产 `paperwritebench-venue-styles`，出处和 sha256 见 `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`）与 `template.tex` 放在一起，所有系统一致；与官方环境里的版本不一定逐字节相同；`paper_3`、`paper_4`、`paper_30`（`[final]` 无赛道选项）和 `paper_12`（`\iclrfinalcopy` 未定义）的模板按原样仍编译不过，不改题目；这次之前的 `paper_1` 运行的版式不作比较 |
| W9 | 复核 agent 的结论取决于它碰巧读了什么：同一批代码细节在不同运行里判法相反（#121） | 官方 `run_evaluation.py` 把整个被评目录（候选的 `template.tex`、`AGENTS.md`、`code/` 等）复制成复核的工作目录 `eval/`，再放进 `gt_main.tex`；pass 1 只给原论文正文，提示要求实现细节去 `code/` 核对。`paper_1` 的 FIFO 半批 buffer（`replay_buffer.py` 的 `deque(maxlen=len(self.items)//2)`）、−0.1 / 1.1 奖励（`experience_maker.py`）、0.2 / 0.35 clip（`loss.py`）都在给系统的代码里，原论文正文里没有。单 agent 运行 `coding-agent-paperwritebench--paper_1-20261028T205750Z`（major 0）的复核读了候选的 `template.tex`，把候选自己的句子当作“GT 明确写道”（如 “bounded capacity (first-in-first-out)”，原论文无此句、候选有）；ResearchWorld 运行 `researchworld-paperwritebench--paper_1-20261030T183318Z`（major 17）的复核只读了 `gt_main.tex` 和表格，没有打开 `code/`，按“GT 里没有 FIFO / 0.35”判 major。我们的目录拼接与官方写作侧的 `latex/` 一致，两次复核的输入相同。按日志里 Read/Grep/Glob/Bash 的路径统计，20 次 PaperWrite-Bench 复核中 2 次读了候选稿、11 次没有碰 `code/` | `paper_1` 的 major 条数混有“复核有没有看代码”的噪声：有代码依据的细节可能被判 major，也可能因误读候选稿而判 supported，两个方向都有；单次的 major 不是写错了的条数 | 标注，不改官方 prompt 和评分规则（#121 不做）；`paper_1` 的 `hallucination_major` 不在运行之间逐条比较，只看汇总并连同 W3、W6；这类 major 要看材料依据时用 `faithfulness-judge` |

## Shared problems

| id | problem | evidence | impact | handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | The judges see neither the material the system was given nor the system's own code and outputs | PaperWritingBench's SxS reads two papers only (official `sxs_paper_quality.py`, `sxs_lit_review_quality.py`); PaperWrite-Bench's hallucination check compares with the original LaTeX only (pass 1 of `evaluate_per_section.py`); ResearchClawBench's judge reads the report, the checklist and images only (`evaluation/score.py`) | Method details the system made up, numbers credited to the wrong method and numbers no code computed go unnoticed, and are sometimes rewarded (P1) | New `faithfulness-judge`: every statement the document makes about its own work is checked against the materials (and an evaluator-side reference). Validation in P1, W3, R1 |
| C2 | The judge models are replaced, with sampling parameters removed | Gemini `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` is served by Antigravity as `gemini-4-argon-high`; the GPT judges (`gpt-4o`, `gpt-5`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5.4`) are served by codex-api as `gpt-5.6-sol`, effort medium; `temperature` and `top_p` are removed (`codex_api.toml`) | A judge's strictness and spread may differ from the official one | Every score records the served model. The substitutes have anchors: PaperWritingBench's SxS of the original against a byte-identical copy of itself gave 8 ties in 8 (the #42 investigation); ScienceAgentBench's figure judge was run with gold, other-task gold and blank predictions on every figure task (S5); ResearchClawBench scores the same report again (R5) |
| C3 | One scoring varies | ResearchClawBench: five scorings of the same report lie between 23.7 and 29.3 (R5); PaperWrite-Bench: the same paper (run R2) scored again moved the rubric from 3.56 to 3.61, major hallucinations from 1 to 4 and claims from 241 to 227 (this Issue); PaperWritingBench: the same paper (run `…-20261028T002600Z`) got literature-review scores of 58 / 57 (Gemini / GPT) in #42 and 51 / 52 when scored again in this Issue; the SxS outcomes were the same both times | A difference of a few points on one item and one scoring means nothing | ResearchClawBench scores every report 2 more times and reports mean, standard deviation and range (`project_checks.repeats`); the other two need 20+ calls per scoring and are compared over many items only |
| C4 | Offline items are not fully cut off: the shield lets the Python package index through | PaperWrite-Bench's official writing agent has no network tools, the ASI-Bench leaderboard page says "no external tool access", PhysClosureBench's `network_access` is `disabled`; here the items of these three benchmarks run with the `offline` shield and additionally let through `GET`/`HEAD` on `pypi.org/simple/` and `files.pythonhosted.org/packages/` (setting `shield.package_index`; every run's `setup.network` states `package_index: allowed`, #105) | The systems under test can install packages with pip and the official agents cannot; the package index holds neither the item's answer nor the paper's content, every other site (literature, papers, code hosting, search) is still 403, and the list rules (original paper, repositories) win over the exception | Recorded in every run's record and on the dashboard; the official scoring is unchanged; read an offline item's result with this network condition in mind |

## PaperWrite-Bench (`paperwritebench-judge`)

| id | problem | evidence | impact | handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | Most of Citation F1 comes from the `references.bib` the system is given | Citing every key of the given bib and writing nothing gives F1 0.756 on average over all 51 papers, median 0.838 (25-paper subset: mean 0.760, median 0.869); for `paper_13` this baseline is 0.613, the two runs 0.673 and 0.646 | F1 mostly measures which bib keys were left out, not the writing | `project_checks.citation`: the cite-everything baseline, the part above it, and F1 with `\cite` in `%` comments removed (the official regex counts keys in comments) |
| W2 | The main hallucination metric is a raw count, and content the original does not state is "neutral", never checked | The official `total_contradictory_major` is a count (`evaluate_per_section.py`), never normalized; run R2 (`coding-agent-paperwritebench--paper_13-20261028T002540Z`) has 241 claims, 31 neutral; the same paper scored again has 227 claims, 37 neutral, and its majors went from 1 to 4 | Shorter papers with fewer claims do better; inventing what the original does not mention costs nothing | `project_checks.hallucination`: major, minor and neutral per 100 claims; grounding in the materials is W3 |
| W3 | The hallucination check never sees the materials, so correct content is judged a major hallucination | The only major of run R1 (`…-20261027T230211Z`) is "the generated description explicitly names gyoza", while the figure the system was given, `figures/description_eg.jpg`, prints "there is a large plate featuring gyoza"; the re-check agent read only the original LaTeX and kept it. The major of run R2 is "the exact model identity for Task 3 is unresolved": the baseline row of the given `table_vs.tex` is identical to the Qwen2-VL-7B row of `table_kf.tex` but labelled Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and the system reported this inconsistency as it is. Scoring R2 again gave 4 majors, these two (gyoza and the model identity) still among them; the other two are "1.5 standard deviations from the class centroid" against "1.5 standard deviations above the class mean" and curve values read from a figure | The 0–1 major per paper are essentially noise, and honest reporting of an inconsistency in the materials is penalized | `faithfulness-judge` (materials include figures and tables, the reference is the original LaTeX): both judges rate these two statements of R2 as backed by the materials; GPT 9 of 121 empirical statements unsupported or contradicted, 0 major (wordings such as "only one run" or "agreement was not measured"); Gemini all 44 backed |
| W4 | Section titles decide what the rubric and the hallucination check cover | The official code classifies sections by keywords (`evaluate_per_section.py`); the original of `paper_13` has no Experiment category, so R2's results under "Results and Analysis" are outside the rubric and the element "Main classification benchmark finding" got 1 ("No classification results are reported"); Conclusion/Discussion sections and sections under 50 words are not checked for hallucinations | Copying the original's section structure scores more; content in Discussion escapes the check | Labelled (changing the classification would change the official scoring) |
| W5 | The rubric scores against the original's elements, checks no correctness and has no length limit | The elements come from the original paper (`eval_points`); the official scoring does not check page counts | Longer papers that follow the original's structure do better | Labelled |
| W6 | The re-check agent can only lower contradictions, and is from the same family as the system under test | Only contradictory claims are re-checked; the re-check is Claude Code `claude-sonnet-4-6` and the coding agent tested is `claude-sonnet-5-5`; the re-check's working directory holds both the prediction and `gt_main.tex` | Self-preference not measured | Labelled; judge and re-check models are recorded in the score |
| W7 | Under `--eval-mode all` a failing re-check leaves the whole evaluation without a result file | Pass 2 of the official `all` mode has no try/except; `hallucination` mode has one | A failed scoring instead of a partial one | Our evaluator raises `ScoreUnavailable` and writes no score when there is no result file; score again |
| W8 | The venue style files the items require are published by neither the official repository nor the dataset | The templates of 51 papers use 14 style files (`neurips_2025`, `cvpr`, `iclr2025_conference` and so on) that the dataset, the PaperRecon repository and stock TeX Live all lack; 46 of the 51 do not compile in a clean TeX Live; yet the PDFs in the official `generated_papers/` are in the venue's layout, and where the official environment gets the styles could not be found (#113); in the existing `paper_1` runs the systems got a directory without them, and some used a stand-in style of their own while others changed the template (see the benchmark README) | The official scoring reads the text of `template.tex`, so the scoring algorithm does not change; what is affected is whether a system can compile the template, and that without a style the layout and page count are not the official ones | New candidate input: the venues' public style package files (asset `paperwritebench-venue-styles`; sources and sha256 in `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`) are placed beside `template.tex` under the names the template uses, the same for every system; not necessarily byte-identical to the official environment's versions; the templates of `paper_3`, `paper_4`, `paper_30` (`[final]` without a track option) and `paper_12` (`\iclrfinalcopy` undefined) still do not compile as given and are not changed; the layout of `paper_1` runs from before this is not compared |
| W9 | The re-check agent's verdict depends on what it happens to read: the same code details are judged in opposite ways in different runs (#121) | The official `run_evaluation.py` copies the whole evaluated directory (the candidate's `template.tex`, `AGENTS.md`, `code/` and so on) into the re-check's working directory `eval/` and adds `gt_main.tex`; pass 1 gets only the original's text, and the prompt tells the agent to check implementation details in `code/`. In `paper_1` the FIFO half-batch buffer (`deque(maxlen=len(self.items)//2)` in `replay_buffer.py`), the −0.1 / 1.1 rewards (`experience_maker.py`) and the 0.2 / 0.35 clip (`loss.py`) are all in the code the system is given and not in the original's text. The re-check of the single-agent run `coding-agent-paperwritebench--paper_1-20261028T205750Z` (major 0) read the candidate's `template.tex` and took the candidate's own sentences as "the GT explicitly states" (such as "bounded capacity (first-in-first-out)", which the original lacks and the candidate has); the re-check of the ResearchWorld run `researchworld-paperwritebench--paper_1-20261030T183318Z` (major 17) read only `gt_main.tex` and the tables, never opened `code/`, and judged major because "the GT has no FIFO / 0.35". Our directory assembly matches the official writing side's `latex/` and the two re-checks had the same inputs. By the Read/Grep/Glob/Bash paths in the logs, of 20 PaperWrite-Bench re-checks 2 read the candidate's paper and 11 never touched `code/` | The major count of `paper_1` carries noise from whether the re-check looked at the code: a detail the code backs can be judged major, or supported through misreading the candidate, in both directions; a single run's major is not the number of wrong statements | Labelled; the official prompt and scoring rules are not changed (out of scope of #121); `hallucination_major` of `paper_1` is not compared claim by claim between runs, only as a total and together with W3 and W6; where the material basis of such a major matters, use `faithfulness-judge` |

run:
  harness: "PaperRecon：launch_writing.py（agent 写论文）+ run_evaluation.py（评分）"
  source: repo README.md '## Usage'；launch_writing.py；run_evaluation.py @1662388
  task_definition: >
    给 agent 一篇论文的 research_overview（short/long）、template.tex（官方设计：带原论文标题、章节标题和导言区，摘要和各节正文为空；paper_13 渲染后的 template.tex 已核对）、references.bib（含摘要）、
    figure/table 摘要与文件、可选代码库；agent 在 LaTeX 中重写整篇论文，再与原文比较。
    source: arXiv 2604.01128 §4.2；paper_recon/common/hf_download.py（目录重建）
  commands:
    fetch_and_write: |
      # --from-hf 默认 hal-utokyo/PaperWrite-Bench，先下载并重建 PaperWrite-Bench/<paper_id>/{original,resources}
      python launch_writing.py --config configs/cc_sonnet46.yaml --paper paper_1 [paper_2 ...]
      python launch_writing.py --config configs/cc_sonnet46.yaml --all   # 见 known_issues
    evaluate: |
      python run_evaluation.py --config-path configs/cc_sonnet46.yaml --paper paper_1 --eval-mode {rubric|hallucination|citation|all}
    source: repo README.md L108-165
  input_format:
    per_paper_dir: "PaperWrite-Bench/<paper_id>/original/{main.tex,main.pdf,config.yaml(type,num_page,column,conference)}; resources/{template.tex,research_overview_short.md,research_overview_long.md,references.bib,figure_summary.txt,table_summary.txt,eval_points.json,figures/,tables/,code/}"
    agent_instructions: "paper_recon/writing/agents_md/AGENTS_{method,benchmark,both}.md 按 config.yaml 的 type 选择"
    source: paper_recon/common/hf_download.py（_reconstruct_paper）；paper_recon/common/config.py（get_agents_md）
  output_format:
    writing: "experiments/<overview_type>/<agent>/<model>/<paper_id>/<timestamp>/{latex/template.tex,pdf/}；带 draftwatermark 'AI-Generated'；编译反馈循环（最多 5 轮 reflection）+ 页数限制调整（最多 10 轮）；launch_writing 默认 3 次重试"
    evaluation: "同目录下 rubric_results_*.json / hallucination_results_*.json / citation_results_*.json / evaluation_results_*.json"
    source: launch_writing.py L108；paper_recon/writing/perform_writeup.py L147,L220；run_evaluation.py L140-175
  official_scorer:
    rubric: >
      每篇论文预置 eval_points.json（按章节的 rubric 要素，GPT-5.4 初生成后作者修订）；
      LLM judge 对每章（Conclusion 除外）每个要素打 1-5 分；图/表另加分项（图上下文分、表匹配分，缺失=1）；
      章节分 = 全部要素均值，总分 = 各章平均。
    hallucination: >
      阶段1：LLM(GPT-5.4) 抽取每章 claim 并分 supported/neutral/contradictory(major/minor)；
      阶段2：contradictory 交由 coding agent（Claude Code，Sonnet 4.6，READONLY，读 GT LaTeX/代码/图表）复核；报告 major contradictory 数量/篇。
    citation: "对 \\cite 键做 F1（纯正则，不调用 LLM）；另报告 hallucinated_keys（不在 bib 中的键）"
    judge_model:
      llm_judge: "azure/gpt-5.4-2026-03-05-azure, temp 1.0（configs/*.yaml 的 evaluation_llm）"
      verification_agent: "ClaudeCode claude-sonnet-4-6, max_turns 20（configs/*.yaml 的 evaluation_agent）"
    source: arXiv 2604.01128 §3.2.2-3.2.4；configs/cc_sonnet46.yaml；paper_recon/evaluation/evaluate_per_section.py L473-565,L676-763,L954-1160；evaluate_citation.py
    human_validation: "rubric 与人类成对判断 Kendall tau_b=0.578 (p<0.001, 24 对)；major contradictory 抽检 96% 为真 (97 例)。source: arXiv §5.3"
  dependencies:
    python: "pixi.toml 固定 python==3.13（pyproject requires-python >=3.14，二者不一致，以 pixi 为准）"
    packages: "litellm, openai, anthropic<0.78, claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.48,<0.2, datasets<4, pymupdf, pymupdf4llm, pypdf, texsoup, tiktoken 等"
    system: "pdflatex+bibtex（代码调用，Dockerfile 装 texlive-full）、chktex、poppler、latexpand；pixi.toml 里为 tectonic/chktex/poppler"
    source: pixi.toml；Dockerfile；paper_recon/writing/perform_writeup.py L73-76
  containers:
    dockerfile: "ubuntu:24.04 + texlive-full + pixi + Claude Code 2.1.77 + Codex 0.115.0；docker-compose.yaml；make up/exec/down；仅 x86_64"
    source: Dockerfile；README.md L53-56,L88-103
  external_services_and_keys:
    items:
      - "被测 agent：Claude Code（CLI 登录）或 Codex/OpenAI（OPENAI_API_KEY 或 Azure）"
      - "评测 judge：GPT-5.4（AZURE_GPT54_API_KEY / AZURE_GPT54_API_BASE，或 OpenAI key，由 config 的 litellm 模型名选择）"
      - "复核 agent：Claude Code Sonnet 4.6"
      - "citation 模式不需要任何 key（本地已验证，见 integrity_check）"
      - "rubric 模式只用 GPT judge，不需要 Claude Code 复核；已用 Codex 网关加占位 key 跑通 oracle（见 integrity_check.oracle_rubric_via_codex_gateway）；hallucination 模式的第二阶段需要 Claude Code 凭据（CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN，只给该进程），已实测 oracle 跑通（见 integrity_check.oracle_hallucination）"
      - "凭据只经环境变量/路径注入，不写入本仓库"
    source: README.md L58-82
  known_issues:
    - issue: "launch_writing.py --all 依赖本地已存在的 PaperWrite-Bench/ 目录；get_paper_names() 在 download_from_hf() 之前执行。静态阅读代码判断：全新检出上 --all 会先遍历不存在目录而失败，需先用 --paper 列出全部 id（或事先 download_from_hf）触发下载；--paper 路径的 get_paper_names 不读目录。未运行验证（运行会启动付费 agent，被权限系统拒绝）。"
      source: launch_writing.py L63-72 与 L136-143
    - issue: "hf_download.DEFAULT_REPO_ID 仍是占位 'your-org/PaperWrite-Bench'；launch_writing 默认值为正确 id，run_evaluation 的 --from-hf const 仍是占位。"
      source: paper_recon/common/hf_download.py L15；run_evaluation.py --from-hf 参数
    - issue: "parquet 元数据含脏字段：paper_46 column='1columnconference: ICML25'，paper_49 column='2columnconference: CVPR25'（config.yaml 写出时会混入）；config.py 用 startswith('2') 判断列数，对二者仍可工作。"
      source: HF test.parquet 元数据列实读（本 manifest integrity_check 的 meta.json）
    - issue: "eval 的 pred 路径约定为 experiments/<short|long>/<Agent>/<model>/<paper>/<ts>/latex/template.tex，外部 agent 需按此落盘或用 --eval-target-dir。"
    - issue: "官方图解析器（evaluate_figure.py）对每个 figure 环境只取一个 \\includegraphics：paper_1 的 GT 里两个 minipage 并排的 figure 环境各丢一张（rethinking.jpg、adv_histogram.jpg），oracle 的图覆盖率因此只有 5/7=0.714；另外 figure_summary.txt 里这两张图的 caption 与实际 caption 对不上（adv_histogram 给了 ssr_eval_curve 的 caption，rethinking 给了 vanishing_adv 的 caption）。rubric 平均分不受影响，但图相关的覆盖分对这类论文会系统性偏低。"
      source: oracle_rubric_via_codex_gateway 运行的 rubric_results 的 figure_coverage；GT main.tex 第 146-160、366-392 行；evaluate_figure.py 图解析段
    - issue: "官方代码用相对路径（PaperWrite-Bench/、experiments/、logs/）并要求工作目录里放这些目录；与 python -I 同用时 paper_recon 需要通过 venv 的 .pth 或安装进 venv 才能导入。"

      source: run_evaluation.py find_latest_experiment_dir / run_evaluation_for_paper

evaluator.text:
# PaperWrite-Bench

[中文](README.md) | English

The machine-readable facts are in [`MANIFEST.yaml`](MANIFEST.yaml). This page covers what a reader needs and points to where each fact lives in the manifest.

## What it is

PaperWrite-Bench (called PaperRecon in the paper) asks an agent to rewrite a whole paper in LaTeX from only the paper's research overview, section skeleton, references, figure/table summaries and optional code, then compares the result with the original. It measures writing quality and hallucination (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.task_definition`; arXiv 2604.01128).

- Paper: arXiv 2604.01128 (source: MANIFEST.yaml `source.paper`).
- Code: `Agent4Science-UTokyo/PaperRecon`, pinned commit `1662388803edf8a891750b272bb7c3dcb430cf3a`, Apache-2.0, redistribution allowed (source: MANIFEST.yaml `source.repo.pinned_commit`, `license.code`).
- Data: Hugging Face `hal-utokyo/PaperWrite-Bench`, pinned revision `781cfdd87191aace9a33c88140116753fd3d53df`, 51 rows in test (source: MANIFEST.yaml `source.dataset`).
- Data licence: there is no single licence; the papers, LaTeX and code belong to their authors, so redistribution must not be assumed. The data stays out of Git; only the source and checksum are recorded (source: MANIFEST.yaml `license.data`).
- Data entry in this repo: asset id `paperwritebench-hf-test-parquet` (`test.parquet`, 745305163 bytes, sha256 in `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`), read through the `assets/paperwritebench-hf-test-parquet` link; it can be downloaded again from HF (source: `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`, that id).

## Subset

25 papers: the two paper-writing benchmarks take 50 papers together, 25 from this one, stratified by paper type (method 16, benchmark 6, both 3) and drawn with the fixed seed 20261028 (maintainer decision of 2026-10-28, Issue #42 comment 6456710905; before that it was all 51 papers). The sampling rule and the list are in MANIFEST.yaml `subset.sampling`; batch file: [`src/tasks/batches/paperwritebench-subset.yaml`](../../batches/paperwritebench-subset.yaml). The other 26 papers can still be run one by one (`paperwritebench/paper_<n>`).

Composition: method 32, benchmark 13, both 6; mostly two-column (source: MANIFEST.yaml `subset.composition`). The task itself needs only CPU (the agent writes and compiles LaTeX); inference happens on the provider side (source: MANIFEST.yaml `subset.per_task_resources.cpu_gpu`).

## How it runs and is scored

- Official entry points: `launch_writing.py` (write the paper) and `run_evaluation.py` (score; `--eval-mode` is `rubric`, `hallucination`, `citation` or `all`) (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.harness`, `run.commands`).
- rubric: each paper has a preset `eval_points.json`; an LLM judge scores each element of each section 1-5, with extra items for figures and tables; the total is the mean over sections (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.rubric`).
- hallucination: an LLM first extracts and classifies the claims of each section, then Claude Code (Sonnet 4.6) re-checks the contradictory claims; the number of major contradictory claims is reported (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.hallucination`).
- citation: F1 over `\cite` keys; pure regex, no LLM call, no key needed (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.citation`).
- The official judge is `azure/gpt-5.4-2026-03-05-azure` (temperature 1.0); the verification agent is `claude-sonnet-4-6` (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.judge_model`).

This project replaces the GPT judge: calls go through the project's Codex gateway, and the model that actually answers is `gpt-5.6-sol`; `temperature` and `max_completion_tokens` are ignored and structured output is only a prompt hint. Scores are therefore not directly comparable with the paper's tables (source: MANIFEST.yaml `credentials.codex_gateway.differences`; PR #9). The verification agent does not go through the gateway and is still Claude Code.

GPT judges now go through codex-api (the Codex gateway was retired in #35); how to run them is in [`USER.en.md`](../../../../USER.en.md), "GPT judges through codex-api". The #8 evidence below was obtained through the old gateway.

Credential variable names (values never enter the repo): the GPT judge uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `AZURE_GPT54_API_KEY` plus `AZURE_GPT54_API_BASE`; through the gateway all three get placeholder values. The hallucination re-check uses `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, passed only to that one subprocess (source: MANIFEST.yaml `credentials.variables`, `credentials.not_env_keys`). For starting the gateway see [`USER.en.md`](../../../../USER.en.md), section "Official benchmark judges"; it is not repeated here.

## One item: what the system gets, how it is scored (Issue #42)

Written `paperwritebench/paper_<n>` (1 to 51); any container system under test can run it:

```bash
uv run researchworld_eval run coding-agent paperwritebench/paper_13 --agent claude --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --effort high \
  --credential anthropic=<variable> --config <settings file>
uv run researchworld_eval providers codex-api start
uv run researchworld_eval score paperwritebench-judge <run-id>
```

- **Given to the system (the candidate side, rendered by `researchworld_eval.benchmarks.paperwritebench`)**: the official
  writer's prompt (`writeup_prompt.py`, with the short overview, the protocol of the published scores) verbatim, with
  nothing of ours added. The official writing directory as it is at `/work`: `template.tex`, `references.bib`,
  `research_overview.md`, `figure_summary.txt` and `table_summary.txt` writable, `figures/`, `tables/` and `code/` mounted
  read-only; the official harness copies the working instructions `AGENTS_<type>.md` to `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code) or
  `AGENTS.md` (Codex) depending on the agent, and here both are placed, so each system reads the one it recognizes. They
  are generated from the parquet at the pinned revision by the rules of the official `_reconstruct_paper` and
  `perform_writeup` (images written as their encoded bytes; the official code re-saves them with PIL). By the official
  design the template carries the original's title, section headings and preamble, the figure and table summaries are the
  original captions, and the tables are the original LaTeX tables.
- **Venue style files** (#113): the venue styles the templates use (`neurips_2025.sty`, `cvpr.sty`,
  `iclr2025_conference.bst`, ...) are shipped by neither the dataset nor the PaperRecon repository, and stock TeX Live
  lacks them (46 of the 51 templates do not compile in a clean TeX Live). The renderer takes the names written in the
  template's `\documentclass`, `\usepackage`, `\RequirePackage` and `\bibliographystyle` and copies the `.sty`/`.cls`/`.bst`
  files of those names from the asset `paperwritebench-venue-styles` (14 files; each file's source, version and sha256 are in
  `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`) into `/work` beside `template.tex`, the same for every system. A style the template does not use
  is not given, and TeX Live's own packages are not in it. The style files are used as published, unmodified.
- **No network**: the official writer has no network tool at all (Claude Code gets only Read/Glob/Grep/Write/Edit; Codex
  has web search off), and all references are in `references.bib`. Here it is the same for every system: the network
  shield is in the `offline` state, every request other than to the model provider and the Python package index (`GET`/`HEAD` on `pypi.org/simple/` and `files.pythonhosted.org/packages/`) gets 403 (rule `offline`), and
  controlled search refuses too. The shield self-check accordingly requires the "allowed site" and OpenAlex probes to be
  stopped by `offline` and the package index page to answer 200. **This differs from the official "no network tool at all"** (#105):
  the package index is let through so that a system can pip-install its own tooling (for example the Agentic Scientist's drafting bootstrap of its evaluator); the index holds neither the item's answer nor the paper's content, and the original paper, repositories and so on are still stopped first by the list.
- **Never given**: `gt_tex`, `gt_pdf`, `eval_points` (it quotes the original verbatim), `research_overview_long` and
  `conference`; the renderer reads only the candidate columns of the parquet.
- **Deliverables**: `/work/template.tex` (the complete paper) and `/work/references.bib`; a PDF is optional and the official
  scoring does not read it.
- **Time limit**: the official harness has no wall-clock limit (its writer gets at most 30 turns); 2 hours per paper
  (maintainer decision of 2026-10-28).
- **Scoring**: the evaluator [`paperwritebench-judge`](../../../evaluators/paperwritebench_judge/README.en.md) runs the
  official `run_evaluation.py --eval-mode all`; the GPT judge goes through codex-api (`gpt-5.6-sol`), the hallucination
  re-check stays Claude Code `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- **The network shield's block list** (offline, it only serves as a record, and the audit still checks the outputs against
  it): the official repository and the HF dataset, and each original paper's arXiv, OpenReview, venue and DOI pages; the
  template carries the original title anyway, so title and authors are not keywords (`title_is_given`) (evaluator-side
  [`shield.yaml`](shield.yaml), 51 papers each verified).

### Differences from the official protocol

After a review against "match the official setting as closely as possible" (maintainer, 2026-10-28):

- Removed: the prompt is the official text verbatim (the first round added Chinese framing, pasted the working
  instructions into the prompt and added a separate note on the bibliography); the working instructions sit in the
  writing directory as `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, as in the official harness; no network (in the first round the system
  could search online through the shield).
- Remaining differences and why:
  - A different writing system: the official writer has only file read/write tools and at most 30 turns, and its
    pipeline does the compiling, 5 reflection rounds "until it compiles" and 10 page-limit rounds; here it is the system
    under test itself, which can compile with its own shell and does not go through the official reflection and page
    rounds. These belong to the official writing system (PaperRecon's writer), not to the task itself.
  - Venue style files: the official repository and dataset publish no style files, and where the official evaluation
    environment gets them from could not be found (the PDFs in the official `generated_papers/` are in the venue's layout,
    so the official environment had them). Here the venues' own public style packages are used (sources in
    `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`) and given under the names the template uses, so they are not necessarily byte-identical to
    the official environment's versions. Where the same name exists for several years only one is taken: `cvpr.sty` is the
    CVPR 2025 version (it differs from the CVPR 2026 one only in the year on the `\ProvidesPackage` line), and `acl.sty` and
    `arxiv.sty` are the default-branch commits at download time. The official scoring reads the text of `template.tex`
    and not the PDF, so the style files decide whether a system can compile the template, not how the score is computed.
  - Four templates still do not compile as given, even with the style files; this is the item itself: `paper_3`, `paper_4`
    and `paper_30` write `\usepackage[final]{neurips_2025}`, and the official style leaves `\@trackname` undefined without a
    track option (`main` and so on), so the footer fails with `Undefined control sequence`; `paper_12` calls `\iclrfinalcopy`
    while loading `arxiv.sty`, which does not define it. The item's content is not changed here; a system that edits the
    template does so on its own, and the run record shows it.
  - Time limit: the official harness has no wall-clock limit; here it is 2 hours per paper.
  - The GPT judge is replaced with `gpt-5.6-sol` (see the evaluator README). The scores are therefore not directly
    comparable with the official published ones.
  - The official prompt and working instructions disagree on the bibliography (an external `references.bib` versus
    `filecontents`); both are given exactly as the official harness has them; scoring reads the external file.

### What the missing style files did to the existing runs (checked in #113, read-only, nothing re-run)

All 31 `paperwritebench` runs in `.project/runs/` of 2026-10-30 were checked. Among the items, only the runs on `paper_1`
(NeurIPS 2025, `[preprint]{neurips_2025}`) are affected; the runs on `paper_13` (`acmart`, shipped with TeX Live) are not.
The `paper_1` runs all predate the style files reaching the candidate side, so the systems got a directory without them:

| --- | --- | --- |
| Agentic Scientist | 6 (`…20261030T000502Z` and others) | 5 failed, 1 stopped, none delivered; the drafting agent records "`neurips_2025.sty` unavailable offline" (#111 smoke); in one (`T092748Z`) the orchestrator's resources hold a `texshim/neurips_2025.sty` compatibility stand-in, which is not the official style |
| Claude Code (coding-agent) | 4 (`…20261028T2057xxZ`) | all completed, `template.tex` still names `neurips_2025`; two tried to download the official style and the `offline` shield stopped them (the shield audit lists `media.neurips.cc` and `raw.githubusercontent.com`); in one the agent says it compiled under a "temporary validation style" and that "official conference-style pagination remains unverified"; 3 of the 4 have no PDF, and two compiles first stopped at the image's missing `inconsolata.sty` (a system-image matter, see #111) |
| EvoScientist | 5 (`…20261028T2002xx`–`T2119xx`) | 3 completed, 2 failed; the agent repeatedly records "`neurips_2025.sty` is not installed" and test-compiles in the container with a stand-in `neurips_2025.sty` of its own (104 bytes in one), so pagination is not the official layout; none has a PDF |
| ResearchWorld | 5 (`…20261028T2256xx`, `T013538Z`, `20261029T202504Z`) | 2 completed (`T225657Z`, `T225703Z`) delivered a `template.tex` that still names `neurips_2025`; 2 stopped with no delivery; the smoke `20261029T202504Z` (completed) delivered a preamble with only `article` (10pt two-column) and no `neurips_2025`, that is, it changed the template. Whether it did so because the style file was missing is not stated in the records and was not established |
| ARC (AutoResearchClaw) | no `paperwritebench` run | — |

Their scores are not changed: the official scoring reads the text of `template.tex` and not the PDF; this only says their layout
is not the official style, so do not read page counts or layout from these runs as a system's ability.

Round 2 shows: the self-check of the `offline` shield passes (the allowed site and OpenAlex are both stopped by `offline`), the official prompt verbatim and `CLAUDE.md` are enough for the system to deliver, and the audit does not count the self-check's `offline` blocks as hits. The conditions of the ResearchWorld rounds are in the [ResearchWorld README](../../../systems/researchworld/README.en.md), "Smoke and calibration results"; the notional cost is estimated at list price from the tokens HuTian records, and #58 recorded it for round 3 only.

Not-verified items closed this time: beyond `paper_1`, a system's output (not the GT) scored in all three official modes.
Still not verified: the other 50 papers; the variance of repeated runs; a side-by-side with the official GPT-5.4 judge.

### Scale and budget

The subset is 25 papers. One sample: 3.1 minutes and 0.46 USD of writing in the first round plus about 6 minutes of
scoring (about 100k judge tokens, about 0.3 USD of re-check). At 5-30 minutes and 0.5-3 USD per paper, 25 papers take
about 2-13 agent hours and 15-75 USD, and about 2.5 hours of serial scoring. The time limit is 2 hours per paper; the
cost cap stays the project default of 1000 USD per run (PR #40; maintainer decision of 2026-10-28).

## Integrity check

#1 (PR #7) built the manifest and ran the offline checks; rubric and hallucination were not run then for lack of a paid judge and were completed by #8 (PR #9). Where the two differ, #8 wins (source: MANIFEST.yaml `integrity_check`; PR #7; PR #9).

| Check | Source | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo HEAD equals the pinned commit (`gh api .../commits/HEAD`) | #1, 2026-10-26 | Pass |
| Paper count is 51 | #1 | Pass |
| Python 3.13 environment build (uv; Python dependencies only) | #1 | Pass |
| Data download sample: rebuild `paper_1`, `paper_5` (binary columns skipped) | #1 | Partial: the full 745 MB was not downloaded; no `main.pdf`, `figures/`, `code/` |
| Oracle citation F1 (GT as prediction, `--eval-mode citation`) | #1 | Pass: `paper_1` 47/47, `paper_5` 57/57, F1 1.0 for both |
| Oracle rubric (official `run_evaluation.py`, Codex gateway, `paper_1`) | #8 | Pass: mean 4.9733 and 5.0 out of 5; 8 calls per run; 129 s and 121 s |
| Oracle hallucination (same, plus Claude Code re-check) | #8 | Pass: all 105 claims supported; 343 s; re-check cost about 0.28 USD |
| Docker image build | - | Not run: the image contains texlive-full and is large |
| `launch_writing.py --all` on a fresh checkout | - | Not run: it would start a paid agent; only a static-reading conclusion exists (see known issues) |

Notes:

- The rubric oracle scored 4.97 to 5.00, which shows the scorer and the gateway path work and do not penalise identical text; the two runs differ by about 0.03, which is judge noise (source: MANIFEST.yaml `integrity_check.oracle_rubric_via_codex_gateway.interpretation`).
- In hallucination, GPT first marked 3 claims contradictory and the Claude Code re-check overturned all of them to supported (source: MANIFEST.yaml `integrity_check.oracle_hallucination.agent_flags`; PR #9).
- Deviation approved by the maintainer: the GPT judge `gpt-5.4` is replaced by `gpt-5.6-sol` (reason: `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the shared file is an empty placeholder and `AZURE_*` does not exist, so the maintainer chose Codex as the GPT provider) (source: PR #9, "偏差").
- Still not verified (as of #8; #42 also ran the three modes on a system's `paper_13`, see above): only `paper_1` was run; no discrimination check on a poor prediction; no side-by-side with the official GPT-5.4; whether the re-check would also overturn a real hallucination is unknown (source: MANIFEST.yaml `integrity_check.oracle_rubric_via_codex_gateway.not_verified`, `integrity_check.oracle_hallucination.not_verified`).

## Published reference scores

Read 2026-10-31 from paper arXiv 2604.01128 Tables 1–3 (v1, the only version): means over all 51 papers for five coding-agent configurations, official pipeline, `short` overview. The judge for rubric and claim extraction is GPT-5.4, the contradictory re-check is Claude Code + Sonnet 4.6; each configuration has one 51-paper mean per metric.

| Agent | Model | Rubric mean (1–5) | Major hallucinations / paper | Citation P / R / F1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Sonnet 4.6 | 3.86 | 10.4 | 0.83 / 0.58 / 0.67 |
| Claude Agent Teams | Sonnet 4.6 | 3.82 | 9.8 | 0.84 / 0.56 / 0.66 |
| Codex | GPT-5.4 | 3.59 | 3.0 | 0.86 / 0.43 / 0.56 |
| Claude Code | Sonnet 4 | 3.49 | 12.0 | 0.75 / 0.24 / 0.34 |
| Codex | GPT-5 | 3.26 | 10.2 | 0.89 / 0.27 / 0.39 |

The main baseline is Claude Code + Sonnet 4.6 (first row). The paper and repository give only 51-paper means; there are no per-paper scores for the 25-paper subset (0/25), so it cannot be recomputed, and the repository holds 255 generated PDFs but no score files. No per-paper wall-clock time, tokens or cost is published, only the writer's `max_turns` of 30 (from the repository configs, honoured by Claude Code only) and no wall-clock limit (source: MANIFEST.yaml `published_scores`).

Differences from the project protocol: the official setup has no wall-clock limit (this project: 2 hours per paper); the agent toolset differs; the judge and model of this project are in each run record (source: MANIFEST.yaml `published_scores.differences_from_our_protocol`).

## Known issues and limits

- The LLM judges' problems and their handling are in W1–W9 of [`../JUDGES.en.md`](../JUDGES.en.md): most of Citation F1 comes from the bib the system is given; hallucinations are a raw count, and the check never sees the materials, so content that is in them can be judged a major hallucination, and whether the re-check agent reads `code/` or takes the candidate's paper for the original varies from run to run (W9: the same code details were judged in opposite ways in the single-agent and the ResearchWorld `paper_1` runs), so the major hallucinations of `paper_1` are read as a total and not compared claim by claim; section titles decide what the rubric covers. Official scores are recorded unchanged; the project's add-on checks (citation baselines, hallucinations per 100 claims, the faithfulness check `faithfulness-judge`) are reported apart from them (Issue #48).
- `launch_writing.py --all` may fail on a fresh checkout (it walks a directory that does not exist yet); this comes from reading the code and was not run (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.known_issues`).
- The `--from-hf` default in `run_evaluation.py` is still a placeholder (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.known_issues`).
- The official figure parser takes only one image per figure environment, so figure coverage for `paper_1` is only 5/7; the rubric mean is not affected (source: MANIFEST.yaml `run.known_issues`).
- The prediction's `references.bib` must be placed alongside, otherwise citation `hallucinated_keys` are all false alarms (source: MANIFEST.yaml `integrity_check.oracle_citation_f1`).
- The total budget is an unverified estimate and needs a pilot run (source: MANIFEST.yaml `subset.total_budget`).
- MANIFEST.yaml `researchworld_integration` is the HuTian interface specification #1 wrote before any run, not updated since (its "the web can reach the original paper" no longer applies). Current state: ResearchWorld has real runs on this benchmark (see "Real run", MANIFEST.yaml `task_interface.real_runs`); the benchmark is offline, and a ResearchWorld run goes through the shield proxy, which lets only the package index through (runs before #105 had no network resource; [ResearchWorld README](../../../systems/researchworld/README.en.md), "Benchmark items"). Candidate gaps are under `researchworld_integration.interface_gaps` and collected in `.agents/knowledge/project/hutian-gaps.md` (source: MANIFEST.yaml `researchworld_integration.current_status`).
- The candidate side must not contain `resources/eval_points.json` or the original paper (source: MANIFEST.yaml `researchworld_integration.separation`).

# PaperWrite-Bench

中文 | [English](README.en.md)

机器可读的事实在 [`MANIFEST.yaml`](MANIFEST.yaml)；本文只说明读者需要知道的内容，并指出每条事实在 manifest 里的位置。

## 是什么

PaperWrite-Bench（论文里叫 PaperRecon）让 agent 只凭论文的研究概述、章节骨架、参考文献、图表摘要和可选代码，用 LaTeX 重写整篇论文，再与原文比较，衡量写作质量和幻觉（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.task_definition`；arXiv 2604.01128）。

- 论文：arXiv 2604.01128（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `source.paper`）。
- 代码：`Agent4Science-UTokyo/PaperRecon`，固定 commit `1662388803edf8a891750b272bb7c3dcb430cf3a`，许可证 Apache-2.0，可再分发（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `source.repo.pinned_commit`、`license.code`）。
- 数据：Hugging Face `hal-utokyo/PaperWrite-Bench`，固定 revision `781cfdd87191aace9a33c88140116753fd3d53df`，test 共 51 行（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `source.dataset`）。
- 数据许可：没有统一许可证；论文、LaTeX 和代码归各作者，不得假设可再分发，所以数据不进 Git，只记录来源和 checksum（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `license.data`）。
- 本仓库的数据入口：资产 id `paperwritebench-hf-test-parquet`（`test.parquet`，745305163 字节，sha256 见 `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`），通过 `assets/paperwritebench-hf-test-parquet` 链接读取；可从 HF 重新下载（来源：`assets/MANIFEST.yaml` 该 id）。

## 子集

用 25 篇：两个写论文 benchmark 合计 50 篇，本 benchmark 25 篇，按论文类型分层（method 16、benchmark 6、both 3），种子 20261028 固定抽样（维护者 2026-10-28 决定，Issue #42 评论 6456710905；此前是全部 51 篇）。抽样规则和名单在 MANIFEST.yaml `subset.sampling`，批次文件：[`src/tasks/batches/paperwritebench-subset.yaml`](../../batches/paperwritebench-subset.yaml)。其余 26 篇仍可单独运行（`paperwritebench/paper_<n>`）。

构成：method 32、benchmark 13、both 6；多数是双栏（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `subset.composition`）。任务本身只用 CPU（agent 只写 LaTeX 并编译），推理在供应商 API 侧（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `subset.per_task_resources.cpu_gpu`）。

## 怎么运行和评分

- 官方入口：`launch_writing.py`（写论文）和 `run_evaluation.py`（评分，`--eval-mode` 取 `rubric`、`hallucination`、`citation`、`all`）（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.harness`、`run.commands`）。
- rubric：每篇有预置的 `eval_points.json`，LLM judge 对每章每个要素打 1-5 分，图表另有加分项；总分是各章平均（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.rubric`）。
- hallucination：先由 LLM 抽取每章 claim 并分类，再由 Claude Code（Sonnet 4.6）复核 contradictory 的 claim，报告 major contradictory 的数量（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.hallucination`）。
- citation：对 `\cite` 键做 F1，纯正则，不调用 LLM，也不需要 key（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.citation`）。
- 官方 judge 是 `azure/gpt-5.4-2026-03-05-azure`（temperature 1.0），复核 agent 是 `claude-sonnet-4-6`（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.official_scorer.judge_model`）。

本项目替换了 GPT judge：经项目的 Codex 网关调用，实际回答的模型是 `gpt-5.6-sol`，`temperature` 和 `max_completion_tokens` 被忽略，结构化输出只作提示。所以分数不能与论文表格直接比较（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `credentials.codex_gateway.differences`；PR #9）。复核 agent 不经网关，仍是 Claude Code。

GPT 判官现在经 codex-api（Codex 网关已在 #35 退役），运行方式见 [`USER.md`](../../../../USER.md)“GPT 判官：经 codex-api”；下面 #8 的证据是经旧网关得到的。

凭据变量名（值不进仓库）：GPT judge 用 `OPENAI_API_KEY`，或 `AZURE_GPT54_API_KEY` 加 `AZURE_GPT54_API_BASE`；经网关时这三个都填占位值。hallucination 的复核用 `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`，只交给该子进程（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `credentials.variables`、`credentials.not_env_keys`）。网关的启动步骤见 [`USER.md`](../../../../USER.md)「benchmark 的官方 judge」一节，这里不重复。

## 一道题：交给系统什么、怎么评分（Issue #42）

写作 `paperwritebench/paper_<n>`（1 到 51），任何容器类被测系统都可以运行：

```bash
uv run researchworld_eval run coding-agent paperwritebench/paper_13 --agent claude --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --effort high \
  --credential anthropic=<变量名> --config <设置文件>
uv run researchworld_eval providers codex-api start
uv run researchworld_eval score paperwritebench-judge <run-id>
```

- **给系统的（候选侧，`researchworld_eval.benchmarks.paperwritebench` 渲染）**：官方写作 agent 的提示（`writeup_prompt.py`，
  用 short 概述，即公开分数的协议）原文，逐字、不加任何我们的说明。官方写作目录原样放在 `/work`：`template.tex`、`references.bib`、
  `research_overview.md`、`figure_summary.txt`、`table_summary.txt` 可写，`figures/`、`tables/`、`code/` 只读挂载；官方把工作
  说明 `AGENTS_<type>.md` 按 agent 复制成 `CLAUDE.md`（Claude Code）或 `AGENTS.md`（Codex），这里两个都放，各系统读自己认的那个。
  这些按官方 `_reconstruct_paper` 和 `perform_writeup` 的规则从固定 revision 的 parquet 生成（图片写原始编码字节，官方用 PIL
  重存）。按官方设计，模板带原论文的标题、章节标题和导言区，图表说明就是原图注，表格是原 LaTeX 表。
- **会议样式文件**（#113）：模板用的会议样式（`neurips_2025.sty`、`cvpr.sty`、`iclr2025_conference.bst` 等）数据集和 PaperRecon 仓库
  都不带，标准 TeX Live 也没有（51 篇里 46 篇的模板在干净的 TeX Live 里编译不过）。渲染时按模板 `\documentclass`、`\usepackage`、
  `\RequirePackage`、`\bibliographystyle` 写的名字，把资产 `paperwritebench-venue-styles`（14 个文件，每个文件的出处、版本和 sha256 见
  `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`）里同名的 `.sty`/`.cls`/`.bst` 复制到 `/work`，与 `template.tex` 同目录，所有系统一样；模板没用到的不给，
  TeX Live 自带的包不在其内。样式文件原样使用、不改动。
- **不联网**：官方写作 agent 没有任何网络工具（Claude Code 只开 Read/Glob/Grep/Write/Edit；Codex 关 web search），参考文献全在
  `references.bib` 里。这里对任何系统都一样：联网屏蔽处于 `offline` 状态，除模型供应商和 Python 包索引（`pypi.org/simple/`、`files.pythonhosted.org/packages/` 的 `GET`/`HEAD`）外的请求一律 403（规则 `offline`），受控
  检索也拒绝。屏蔽自检相应地要求“允许的网站”和 OpenAlex 探针都被 `offline` 拦下，包索引页返回 200。**这和官方“没有任何网络工具”不同**（#105）：
  放行包索引，是为了让系统能 pip 装自己的工具（例如 Agentic Scientist 的起草评测器引导步骤）；包索引不含题目答案，也不含论文内容，原论文、仓库等照旧先被屏蔽表挡住。
- **不给的**：`gt_tex`、`gt_pdf`、`eval_points`（含原论文原文证据）、`research_overview_long`、`conference`；渲染只读 parquet
  的候选列。
- **交付物**：`/work/template.tex`（完整论文）和 `/work/references.bib`；PDF 可选，官方评分不读。
- **时间上限**：官方没有墙钟上限（写作 agent 最多 30 轮）；每篇 2 小时（维护者 2026-10-28 决定）。
- **评分**：评测系统 [`paperwritebench-judge`](../../../evaluators/paperwritebench_judge/README.md) 用官方 `run_evaluation.py
  --eval-mode all`，GPT judge 经 codex-api（`gpt-5.6-sol`），hallucination 复核仍是 Claude Code `claude-sonnet-4-6`。
- **联网屏蔽的名单**（离线时只剩记录意义，审计仍按它检查产出）：官方仓库和 HF 数据集，以及每篇原论文的 arXiv、OpenReview、会议页和
  DOI；模板本来就带原标题，所以标题和作者不作关键词（`title_is_given`）（评测侧 [`shield.yaml`](shield.yaml)，51 篇逐条核实）。

### 与官方协议的差异

按“尽可能与官方设置一致”（维护者 2026-10-28）复查后：

- 已消除：提示是官方原文（第一轮外加中文说明、把工作说明贴进提示并就参考文献写法另作说明）；工作说明按官方以 `CLAUDE.md` /
  `AGENTS.md` 放在写作目录；不联网（第一轮可以经屏蔽联网检索）。
- 仍有的差异和原因：
  - 写作系统不同：官方写作 agent 只有读写文件的工具、最多 30 轮，编译、5 轮“直到能编译”的反思和 10 轮页数调整由流水线做；这里是
    被测系统自己，可以用 shell 自己编译，不经官方的反思和页数轮次。这些属于官方的写作系统（PaperRecon 的 writer），不是题目本身。
  - 会议样式文件：官方仓库和数据集没有发布样式文件，官方评测环境从哪里取得它们查不到（官方 `generated_papers/` 里的 PDF 是会议排版，
    说明官方环境里有）。这里改用各会议官方发布的公开样式包（来源见 `assets/MANIFEST.yaml`），照模板所用的名字提供，因而与官方环境里的版本
    不一定逐字节相同。年份不同的同名文件只取一个：`cvpr.sty` 取 CVPR 2025 版（与 CVPR 2026 版只差 `\ProvidesPackage` 一行的年份），
    `acl.sty` 和 `arxiv.sty` 取下载时的主分支提交。官方评分读 `template.tex` 的文本、不读 PDF，所以样式文件影响的是系统能否按模板
    编译，不影响分数的算法。
  - 即使有了样式文件，4 篇的模板按原样仍编译不过，属于题目本身：`paper_3`、`paper_4`、`paper_30` 写 `\usepackage[final]{neurips_2025}`，
    官方样式在没有赛道选项（`main` 等）时不定义 `\@trackname`，页脚报 `Undefined control sequence`；`paper_12` 调用 `\iclrfinalcopy`，
    而它加载的是 `arxiv.sty`、没有定义。这里不改题目内容；系统自己改模板是系统的做法，记入运行记录。
  - 时间上限：官方没有墙钟上限，这里每篇 2 小时。
  - GPT judge 被替换为 `gpt-5.6-sol`（见评测系统 README）。分数因此不与官方公开分数直接可比。
  - 官方提示和工作说明对参考文献写法不一致（外部 `references.bib` 与 `filecontents`），照官方原样给出；评分读外部文件。

### 缺样式文件对已有运行的影响（#113 核对，只读，不重跑）

核对 2026-10-30 `.project/runs/` 里全部 31 次 `paperwritebench` 运行。题目里只有 `paper_1`（NeurIPS 2025，`[preprint]{neurips_2025}`）的运行受影响；
`paper_13`（`acmart`，TeX Live 自带）的运行不受影响。`paper_1` 的运行都在样式文件进入候选侧之前，系统拿到的是没有样式文件的目录：

子集 25 篇。单个样本：第一轮 3.1 分钟、0.46 美元（写作）+ 约 6 分钟打分（判官约 10 万 token，复核约 0.3 美元）。按每篇 5–30 分钟、
0.5–3 美元估计，25 篇约 2–13 个 agent 小时、15–75 美元，打分约 2.5 小时（串行）。时间上限每篇 2 小时；费用上限沿用项目默认的每次
运行 1000 美元（PR #40；维护者 2026-10-28 决定）。

## 已知问题和限制

- LLM 判官的问题和处理见 [`../JUDGES.md`](../JUDGES.md) 的 W1–W9：Citation F1 大部分来自给系统的 bib；幻觉是原始计数，且看不到材料，材料里有的内容也会被判为重大幻觉，复核 agent 有没有读 `code/`、会不会把候选稿当作原论文都因运行而异（W9，同一批代码细节在单 agent 和 ResearchWorld 的 `paper_1` 运行里判法相反），所以 `paper_1` 的重大幻觉只看汇总、不逐条比较；rubric 的范围由章节标题决定。官方分数照录，本项目的附加检查（引用基线、每百条 claim 的幻觉、忠实度检查 `faithfulness-judge`）与官方分数分开报告（Issue #48）。
- `launch_writing.py --all` 在全新检出上可能失败（先遍历不存在的目录），静态阅读得出，未运行验证（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.known_issues`）。
- `run_evaluation.py` 的 `--from-hf` 仍是占位默认值（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.known_issues`）。
- 官方图解析器每个 figure 环境只取一张图，`paper_1` 的图覆盖率因此只有 5/7；rubric 平均分不受影响（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `run.known_issues`）。
- 预测的 `references.bib` 必须一起放好，否则 citation 的 `hallucinated_keys` 全部误报（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `integrity_check.oracle_citation_f1`）。
- 总预算是未验证的估计，需要 pilot 实测（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `subset.total_budget`）。
- MANIFEST.yaml `researchworld_integration` 是 #1 在运行前写的 HuTian 接口规格，没有随实现更新（其中“联网可检索原论文”已不适用）。现状：ResearchWorld 已在本 benchmark 上真实运行（见“真实运行”、MANIFEST.yaml `task_interface.real_runs`）；本 benchmark 离线，ResearchWorld 运行经屏蔽代理，只放行包索引（#105 之前的运行没有网络资源；[ResearchWorld README](../../../systems/researchworld/README.md)“benchmark 题目”）。缺口候选见 `researchworld_integration.interface_gaps`，汇总在 `.agents/knowledge/project/hutian-gaps.md`（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `researchworld_integration.current_status`）。
- 候选侧不能带 `resources/eval_points.json` 和原论文（来源：MANIFEST.yaml `researchworld_integration.separation`）。

conditions.name: RW-sonnet
conditions.description: ResearchWorld：E2E 任务用全部 9 个岗位；benchmark 题目按 HuTian 官方 benchmark 设置选岗位；所有岗位同一模型
conditions.description_en: ResearchWorld: all 9 roles for E2E tasks; benchmark items take the roles of HuTian's own benchmark settings; the same model in every role

system.name: researchworld
system.description: HuTian ResearchWorld 4.8.2, this project's own install (images :rwe-v4.8.2)

agent.name: Claude Code
agent.how: one agent per role through acpx's ACP adapter in the role's sandbox container

network.search: the shared search tool (MCP server rwe-search in every sandbox) through the same shield
network.web_access: every request of every role through the run's shield proxy, HuTian's mandatory upstream proxy with the shield's CA: the same URL, keyword, id and date rules as the other systems, the shield logs each URL; no direct way out, server-side search and remote tools off (Issue #73)

tools.permissions: acpx --approve-all --non-interactive-permissions fail: every tool call the agent asks for is approved; the role's sandbox container is the boundary

preinstalled.zh: HuTian 的 system image researchworld:rwe-v4.8.2 和 worker image researchworld-worker:rwe-v4.8.2（acpx 与各 agent 的 ACP 适配、researchworld 包的 Python、Node.js）
preinstalled.en: HuTian's system image researchworld:rwe-v4.8.2 and worker image researchworld-worker:rwe-v4.8.2 (acpx and each agent's ACP adapter, Python with the researchworld packages, Node.js)

reasons.resources.cpus: world.json sets no resources: each role's sandbox gets HuTian's defaults
reasons.limits.time_limit_hours: the world configuration sets no budget.total_seconds: `run --hours` or the run's settings file sets it

notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].

Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator has its run's private docker socket; the privileged daemon is root-equivalent.

preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
notes.credentials: The provider key is in the process environment and EvoScientist's execute shell inherits the environment (upstream has no switch); the key is therefore visible to the agent's shell. It is a run-scoped copy and is not logged by this adapter.
notes.memory: A fresh data dir per run (baked skills, empty memory). Memory workers, skill synthesis and the scheduler stay at upstream defaults, so their LLM calls count in the usage log.
notes.limits: async sub-agents off (README advice for scripted runs); recursion_limit=1000000; model retry wait in auto-mode 1800 s (time without progress counts as wall time); execute timeout 300 s per command. No token or cost budget exists.
